newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -BTP, Bund vols edgy as futures look toppy.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -BTP, Bund vols edgy as futures look toppy.

text.p: Implied volatility of BTP and Bund options traded on LIFFE were broadly unchanged but jittery in early trade on Tuesday, as traders said the underlying futures were looking overpriced.
Bund futures rallied at the open, with the June futures up 0.30 at 100.21 by 1018 GMT. Italian BTP futures were also higher, up 0.46 at 128.63.
"BTPs are defying gravity at the moment," said a trader at a European bank on the LIFFE floor. "And although Bunds were due a bit of a kick higher, the volume isn't really good enough to back it up."

Brokers quoted June Bund volatility at 5.50 percent, slightly higher bid from 5.45 percent on Monday. May volatility was attracting little interest, as the options expire on April 23. June BTP option volatility was at 7.55 percent off slightly from 7.60 percent earlier, brokers said.
Traders said a good rule of thumb is that one percentage point of volatility is equal to about six ticks of anticipated movement in the underlying future.
That would imply that the market is expecting daily moves of about 32 ticks in the Bund future.

"It's interesting to note that while Bunds are at the top end of their recent volatility range, BTPs are near the bottom," said a trader at a French bank in London. "The spread looks like a worthwhile trade at the moment."

In BTPs, the June 132.00 strike calls were active, which traders said were "punts" rather than strategic trades. With 26 days until the June options expire, traders said the calls have a "reasonable chance" of making money.
